finding: Harness controls capability/environment, loops produce correction evidence, and graphs expose candidate flow; only 036 authorizes mutation even when GraphARC confines routes.

Task-node spawn/cancel/reorder can form a newly admitted work-graph proposal, while adding tool access is capability escalation requiring renewed identity, policy, gate, budget, and 036 authorization.

Builder-Judge-Manager loops need structured external ground truth and hard stops; cap/time/cost termination is incomplete or escalated, never convergence, and concurrent loops need aggregate budget authority.

The multi-factor DAG is a useful governance fixture and explicitly exposes advisory spend, but statistical gates and local metering do not establish tradable alpha, hard budget, data lineage, risk authority, or effect permission.
Fresh child context, predeclared returns, deterministic checks, and sandboxing reduce contamination but do not prove independent provenance, reserve shared budget, fence writes, or authorize commits.

Work orchestration, supervising loops, and knowledge retrieval require distinct schemas and owners; GraphARC implements work execution and observational replay, not a governed GraphRAG or canonical fact store.
Repair harness or loop failures at their owning layer and formalize a graph only after observed stable dependencies show a need for specialists, parallelism, gates, recovery, or pause/resume.
